hygiene.meta_title: Dental Cleaning Plateau Mont-Royal | Scaling & Hygiene
hygiene.meta_description: Professional teeth cleaning, scaling and periodontal check-ups on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Personalized prevention for healthy gums and a lasting smile.
hygiene.hero_subtitle: The best dentistry is the kind you never need. Our preventive protocols keep your gums healthy and catch problems before they escalate.
hygiene.description: Healthy gums are the foundation of a beautiful smile and strong teeth. At every periodic check-up, our hygienist removes tartar and plaque that brushing can't reach, assesses your gum health and guides you toward a personalized home hygiene routine. We also screen for gum recession, dentin hypersensitivity, parafunction habits like bruxism, and defective fillings — all conditions that are much easier to address early.
features: Elimination of gum inflammation and periodontal pockets
Detection and correction of traumatic occlusion
Treatment of gum recession and hypersensitivity

faq.q: How often should I get a dental cleaning?
faq.a: For most patients, every 6 months is sufficient. If you tend to accumulate tartar quickly or have a history of gum disease, we recommend every 3 to 4 months.

faq.q: Is scaling painful?
faq.a: Scaling is generally painless. If your gums are sensitive, we can apply a topical anesthetic gel for your comfort before starting.

faq.q: Does my insurance cover dental cleanings?
faq.a: Most dental insurance plans cover 1 to 2 cleanings per year. We help you maximize your coverage at every visit.

faq.q: Are dental cleanings covered by the CDCP?
faq.a: Yes, the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) covers prophylactic cleanings and periodontal assessments for eligible beneficiaries. We submit the claim directly at your visit.

faq.q: How do I know if I have gum disease?
faq.a: The most common signs are gums that bleed when you brush, persistent bad breath, red or swollen gums, and teeth that appear to be 'getting longer' (gum recession). If you notice any of these, book an appointment soon — periodontal disease responds well to treatment when caught early.

veneers.meta_title: Porcelain Veneers Plateau Mont-Royal | Cosmetic Dentistry
veneers.meta_description: Ultra-thin ceramic veneers (0.3 mm) and invisible composite fillings on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Correct colour, shape and gaps with minimal tooth preparation.
veneers.hero_subtitle: Precise, ultra-natural corrections to give you a smile you are proud to show — without compromising the structure of your teeth.
veneers.description: Porcelain veneers are thin ceramic shells (as thin as 0.3 mm) bonded to the visible surface of your teeth to correct colour, shape, mild misalignment or gaps. They require minimal tooth reduction and deliver an exceptionally natural result. Cosmetic composite fillings, meanwhile, replace old grey amalgam restorations and treat cavities invisibly — no one will know the difference. The result is a harmonious smile where the work simply cannot be detected.
features: Correction of colour, shape and diastemas
Natural, long-lasting result (10–15 years for veneers)

faq.q: Do porcelain veneers damage your teeth?
faq.a: Ultra-thin veneers (0.3 mm) require very little — sometimes zero — tooth preparation. They are considered the least invasive option in cosmetic dentistry.

faq.q: How long do veneers last?
faq.a: With proper care (brushing, flossing, regular check-ups), porcelain veneers typically last 10 to 15 years.

faq.q: How many appointments are needed for veneers?
faq.a: Generally 2 to 3 visits: consultation and digital planning, preparation and digital impression, then final placement.

faq.q: Are porcelain veneers covered by dental insurance?
faq.a: Purely cosmetic veneers are generally not covered by insurance. However, if a veneer is replacing a fractured or damaged tooth, partial coverage may apply. We help you check your benefits at the consultation.

faq.q: Can you whiten porcelain veneers?
faq.a: No — ceramic restorations do not respond to whitening agents. If you want a brighter smile, teeth whitening should be done before veneers are placed so the shade of the entire smile can be matched.

rootCanal.meta_title: Root Canal Plateau Mont-Royal | Painless Endodontics & Crown
rootCanal.meta_description: Painless root canal therapy at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Precise endodontic treatment and metal-free ceramic crown to save your natural tooth.
rootCanal.hero_subtitle: Saving your natural tooth is always our first priority. Modern root canal treatment is fast, precise and far more comfortable than you might expect.
rootCanal.description: When the pulp inside a tooth (the living tissue) is infected or irreparably damaged by deep decay or trauma, root canal therapy is the solution to save the tooth without extracting it. We meticulously clean the root canals, disinfect them and seal them hermetically. In the vast majority of cases, a devitalized tooth should then be protected by a metal-free ceramic crown — highly fracture-resistant — which restores its shape and function while preserving aesthetics.
features: Endodontic therapy under local anesthesia — pain-free
Thorough cleaning and hermetic sealing of canals

faq.q: Is a root canal painful?
faq.a: No. Under modern local anesthesia, root canal treatment is no more uncomfortable than a regular filling. It's the pre-existing infection that causes pain — the treatment relieves it.

faq.q: Do I always need a crown after a root canal?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. A devitalized tooth becomes brittle and prone to fracture. A crown protects it and restores its full strength.

faq.q: How long does root canal treatment take?
faq.a: Most treatments are completed in 1 to 2 appointments. Complex cases (curved canals, retreatment) may require 3 sessions.

faq.q: Can I drive or go back to work after a root canal?
faq.a: Yes. The treatment is done under local anesthesia; once it wears off (2 to 3 hours), you can drive and resume normal activities. We recommend avoiding hard foods for the rest of the day.

faq.q: What if my tooth still hurts after the root canal?
faq.a: Mild sensitivity for a few days after treatment is normal. If the discomfort persists beyond a week or intensifies, contact us — it may be residual inflammation or an additional canal that needs attention. A quick follow-up visit resolves it.

implants.meta_title: Dental Implants in Montreal | Plateau Mont-Royal
implants.meta_description: Dental implant placement on the Plateau Mont-Royal. The permanent, natural-looking solution to replace missing teeth — biocompatible and built to last.
implants.hero_subtitle: A dental implant is the closest thing to a real tooth — beautiful, fully functional and designed to last a lifetime.
implants.description: A dental implant is an artificial root made of biocompatible titanium placed directly into the jawbone. Once osseointegration is complete (3 to 6 months), a custom ceramic crown is attached to the implant to recreate the visible tooth. Unlike bridges, an implant does not require grinding down adjacent teeth. It preserves bone, is cared for just like a natural tooth, and offers results that can last decades. For patients with full or partial dentures, mini-implants can stabilize a removable prosthesis and eliminate unsightly clasps.
features: Implant-supported bridge for multiple missing teeth

faq.q: Am I a candidate for a dental implant?
faq.a: Most healthy adults are candidates. A 3D cone beam scan evaluates available bone volume. In some cases, a bone graft may be needed beforehand.

faq.q: Is implant placement painful?
faq.a: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is generally well-tolerated. Post-operative effects are similar to those of an extraction: mild sensitivity and swelling for 48–72 hours.

faq.q: How long does a dental implant last?
faq.a: With proper maintenance (brushing, flossing, annual check-ups), an implant can last 20 to 30 years — often a lifetime.

faq.q: How much does a dental implant cost in Montreal?
faq.a: The cost of an implant varies by clinical situation, but typically ranges from $2,500 to $4,500 for the implant and crown combined. A consultation with a 3D radiographic assessment is needed for a precise quote. We also help you determine whether your insurance or the CDCP can cover part of the cost.

faq.q: Are dental implants covered by the CDCP?
faq.a: The CDCP covers certain surgical acts related to implants depending on your coverage tier and clinical situation. At your consultation, we verify your eligibility and submit the claim on your behalf.

orthodontics.meta_title: Invisalign Plateau Mont-Royal | Invisible Orthodontics Adults & Teens
orthodontics.meta_description: Straighten your teeth discreetly with Invisalign on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Metal-free orthodontics for adults and teenagers. Free Invisalign consultation.
orthodontics.hero_subtitle: Align your teeth without brackets, without metal, without aesthetic compromise — at your pace, with custom clear aligners.
orthodontics.description: Invisalign® is the world's most advanced invisible orthodontic system. Each series of clear aligners is custom-made from a digital impression (Trios 3D scanner) and progressively moves your teeth toward the computer-planned target position. The aligners are removable — take them out to eat and brush your teeth — and virtually invisible, making them ideal for adults and teens who care about their appearance. We show you a virtual preview of your final smile before treatment even begins.
features: Invisalign® clear aligners — discreet and comfortable
3D digital planning with final smile preview

faq.q: How long does Invisalign treatment take?
faq.a: A mild case can be completed in 6 to 12 months. More complex cases take 18 to 24 months. The exact duration is determined at your initial consultation.

faq.q: Is Invisalign as effective as traditional braces?
faq.a: For the majority of cases, yes. Invisalign effectively treats moderate crowding, gaps and mild to moderate malocclusion. Very severe cases may still require braces.

faq.q: How much does Invisalign cost?
faq.a: Costs vary by case complexity (approximately $3,500 to $7,000). We offer an initial consultation to assess your case and provide an accurate quote.

faq.q: Does insurance cover Invisalign?
faq.a: Some dental insurance plans include partial orthodontic coverage (braces or Invisalign), often between $1,000 and $2,500 lifetime maximum. We help you maximize your benefits at the consultation.

faq.q: Do I need retainers after Invisalign?
faq.a: Yes — retainers are essential to maintain your results. We custom-fabricate them at the end of your treatment. Worn at night, they keep your teeth in their new position long-term.

surgery.meta_title: Oral Surgery Plateau Mont-Royal | Tooth Extraction & Gum Graft
surgery.meta_description: Tooth extractions, gum grafts and implant surgery on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Precise, gentle surgical care for fast recovery.
surgery.hero_subtitle: When surgery is needed, our minimally invasive techniques and careful approach ensure your comfort and a smooth, speedy recovery.
surgery.description: Our oral surgery services cover the extraction of severely compromised or highly mobile teeth (in advanced periodontal disease), implant placement, and gum grafts to treat recession or congenital absence of attached gingiva. All procedures are performed under local anesthesia using minimally invasive techniques and, where possible, assisted by our Bluewave laser to reduce bleeding and accelerate healing.
features: Extraction of severely damaged or fractured teeth
Extraction of highly mobile teeth (periodontal disease)
Gum graft (recession or congenital absence of gingiva)
Treatment of root hypersensitivity through tissue grafting
Bluewave laser assistance for reduced bleeding

faq.q: Are tooth extractions painful?
faq.a: Extractions are performed under local anesthesia and should not be painful during the procedure. Post-operative discomfort (24–48h) is managed with standard pain relievers.

faq.q: What is a gum graft?
faq.a: It is a procedure where gingival tissue (taken from the palate or a tissue bank) is grafted onto a recession area to cover the exposed root and prevent sensitivity and bone loss.

faq.q: How long is recovery after oral surgery?
faq.a: For a simple extraction, 24–48 hours. For a gum graft or implant placement, expect 3 to 7 days before returning to normal activity.

faq.q: Can I eat normally after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: Avoid hard, hot foods and straws for the first 24 hours to protect the blood clot. Stick to soft foods (soups, yogurt, mashed potatoes). You can generally resume normal eating after 48 to 72 hours.

faq.q: Is a gum graft painful?
faq.a: The procedure is performed under local anesthesia and is not painful during surgery. Mild to moderate post-operative discomfort (palate tenderness, slight swelling) is common for 3 to 5 days and is managed with standard pain relievers.

radiology.meta_title: Digital Dental X-Ray Plateau Mont-Royal | Panoramic & Cone Beam 3D
radiology.meta_description: 100% digital dental radiology on the Plateau Mont-Royal. Planmeca panoramic, intraoral sensors and 3D cone beam for precise diagnostics with minimal radiation.
radiology.hero_subtitle: Sharper images, more accurate diagnoses, and up to 90% less radiation than conventional equipment — for your health and the environment.
radiology.description: Digital radiology is at the heart of our diagnostic approach. Our Planmeca panoramic unit and digital intraoral sensors produce high-resolution images instantly available on screen — no developing time, no chemicals. Radiation dose is reduced by up to 90% compared to analogue equipment. For implant planning or complex case evaluation, our 3D cone beam provides a complete three-dimensional view of bone and dental structures.
features: 3D cone beam imaging for implant planning
Up to 90% less radiation vs analogue

faq.q: Are dental X-rays dangerous?
faq.a: With our digital technology, the radiation dose is extremely low — comparable to a few hours of cosmic radiation during a flight. The diagnostic benefits far outweigh the risk.

faq.q: How often should I have dental X-rays?
faq.a: For a healthy adult with no risk factors: a panoramic X-ray every 3–5 years and bitewing X-rays every 1–2 years during routine exams.

faq.q: What is a cone beam CT scan?
faq.a: It is a dental scanner that produces a full 3D reconstruction of your jaws and teeth. Essential for precisely planning implant placement or evaluating complex cases.

faq.q: Are dental X-rays covered by insurance?
faq.a: Yes — diagnostic X-rays (bitewings, panoramic) are generally covered by dental insurance plans at defined intervals (e.g., bitewings every 1–2 years). We submit the claim directly to your insurer.

faq.q: Can pregnant women have dental X-rays?
faq.a: With our digital technology, the radiation dose is extremely low. When clinically necessary (pain, infection), X-rays can be taken with a lead apron for protection. We recommend postponing routine X-rays to the second trimester or after delivery whenever possible.

whitening.meta_title: Teeth Whitening Plateau Mont-Royal | Professional Results
whitening.meta_description: Professional teeth whitening at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Visible, lasting results with minimal sensitivity. Achieve a brighter smile safely.
whitening.hero_subtitle: A smile several shades brighter in one session — with safe, dentist-supervised products that deliver results that last.
whitening.description: Professional teeth whitening is the safest and most effective way to brighten your smile. Unlike over-the-counter kits, our protocols use optimal-concentration whitening agents tailored to your teeth and applied under dental supervision. We offer two formats: in-office whitening (immediate results in one hour) and take-home whitening with custom-fitted trays (for a gradual treatment at your own pace). Both options can be combined for maximum impact.
features: Visible results of 4 to 8 shades lighter
Post-treatment fluoride protocol for lasting brightness

faq.q: Is teeth whitening safe?
faq.a: Yes, when performed under dental supervision with appropriate products. We first assess your gum health and enamel condition to tailor the protocol to your situation.

faq.q: How long do whitening results last?
faq.a: On average 1 to 3 years depending on your dietary habits (coffee, tea, red wine, tobacco). Occasional touch-ups with the custom trays help maintain brightness.

faq.q: Does whitening work on crowns and veneers?
faq.a: No — ceramic and composite restorations do not respond to whitening agents. We plan the treatment to harmonize the overall shade of your smile.

faq.q: Is professional teeth whitening covered by insurance?
faq.a: No — teeth whitening is considered a cosmetic procedure and is not covered by standard dental insurance. That said, the results of a professional whitening are significantly superior to over-the-counter kits, often at a comparable price point.

faq.q: At what age can you start teeth whitening?
faq.a: We recommend waiting until all adult teeth have fully erupted, generally from age 16 to 18. Before that age, enamel is still developing and whitening is not advisable.

technology.meta_title: Advanced Dental Technology Plateau Mont-Royal | 3D Scanner, Laser
technology.meta_description: Trios 3D oral scanner, Bluewave diode laser and full digital radiology at Centre Dentaire du Plateau. Technology in service of more precise and comfortable care.
technology.hero_title: Advanced Technology in Service of Your Smile
technology.hero_subtitle: We continuously invest in the latest innovations so that every treatment is more accurate, faster and more comfortable for you.
technology.description: Modern technology is radically transforming the dental experience. Our Trios oral scanner (3Shape) replaces unpleasant impression pastes with a digital scan in seconds — more precise and instantly transmittable to the laboratory. Our Bluewave diode laser treats soft tissue (gums) without bleeding, without sutures in most cases, and accelerates healing. Our fully digital radiology (panoramic + intraoral sensors + 3D cone beam) reduces radiation exposure and improves diagnostic quality. Together, these technologies enable less invasive, more predictable care and consistently high-quality results.
features: Trios 3D oral scanner — digital impressions, no paste
Bluewave diode laser for soft tissue (no scalpel)
3D cone beam imaging for implant surgery

faq.q: What is a Trios oral scanner?
faq.a: It is a device that captures a 3D digital impression of your teeth in minutes — no paste, no discomfort. The data is sent directly to the dental lab to fabricate crowns, veneers and aligners with sub-millimetre precision.

faq.q: Does the dental laser replace the drill?
faq.a: The Bluewave diode laser is used specifically for soft tissue (gums). It does not replace the drill for cavity treatment, but it allows gum procedures (reshaping, periodontal treatment) without a scalpel and with less post-operative discomfort.

faq.q: Do these technologies increase the cost of care?
faq.a: Some technologies carry a slightly higher cost (e.g. digital vs conventional impression), but they often reduce the number of appointments needed and improve precision, which avoids costly remakes.

faq.q: Is a digital impression (Trios scanner) more accurate than a traditional one?
faq.a: Yes — digital impressions have sub-millimetre accuracy, eliminate distortions from impression paste, and are transmitted instantly to the lab. This means better-fitting crowns, veneers and aligners, and fewer adjustment appointments.

faq.q: What is Digital Smile Design (DSD)?
faq.a: Digital Smile Design is a planning software that simulates your final smile on screen before any treatment begins. It lets you visualize the expected result for veneers, implants or orthodontic work, and helps us design a smile that fits your face and preferences.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before your visit.

new_patients.question: First visit or new to Canada?
new_patients.answer: We warmly welcome new patients and people who have recently arrived in Canada. During your first visit, we perform a complete oral health assessment (clinical exam + X-rays) to establish your personalized treatment plan. Our multilingual team guides you through all administrative steps: enrolling in insurance, using the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP), and understanding your coverage. You don't need to prepare anything — we take care of everything.

cdcp.question: Do you accept the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)?
cdcp.answer: Yes, we are a CDCP partner. This federal program is open to all Canadian residents without private dental insurance whose family net income is under $90,000/year. It covers a wide range of services: exams, cleanings, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions and more. To benefit, register at canada.ca, then present your membership card at your appointment — we submit the claim directly. Coverage renews annually after you file your income tax return.

payment.question: What are your payment methods?
payment.answer: We accept credit cards, checks, and cash. We also work with most insurance providers for direct billing.

emergency.question: How to handle a weekend emergency?
emergency.answer: For emergencies outside our opening hours (Mon–Thu 9am–6pm, Fri 9am–2pm), leave a voicemail at 514 528-1587 — we call you back as a priority at opening. For cases that cannot wait, you may also consult a local emergency dental service.

languages.question: Do you speak other languages?
languages.answer: Yes, our team communicates in French, English, and Tagalog. We make sure every patient fully understands their treatment plan, regardless of language.

insurance_direct.question: Can you bill my insurance directly?
insurance_direct.answer: Yes, we offer direct billing with most private insurance providers. Just bring your insurance card to your appointment and we handle the submission — you only pay the portion not covered by your plan.

children.question: Do you accept children?
children.answer: Absolutely — we treat patients of all ages, from toddlers to seniors. Our dentists are experienced in making children feel comfortable and explaining procedures in a fun, engaging way to build healthy habits from an early age.

ramq.question: Does the RAMQ cover dental care?
ramq.answer: The RAMQ covers basic dental care for children under 10 (exams, cleanings, fillings, extractions). For adults, the RAMQ generally does not cover dental care, except in rare cases such as certain oral surgeries performed in a hospital setting. If you have no private insurance, the federal Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) may cover a large portion of your costs — we are a registered CDCP provider.

items.title: Severe toothache
items.desc: Acute, throbbing, or nocturnal pain — often a sign of infection. Quick treatment to relieve pain.

items.title: Dental abscess
items.desc: Swelling, fever, discharge: a medical emergency that cannot wait.

items.title: Knocked-out tooth (trauma)
items.desc: Keep the tooth in milk or under your tongue and call immediately — every minute counts.

items.title: Lost crown or filling
items.desc: Extreme sensitivity or functional discomfort: we recement or protect the tooth without delay.

items.title: Dental bleeding
items.desc: Post-extraction or traumatic bleeding that won't stop — contact us right away.

items.title: Painful wisdom tooth

items.title: Broken appliance or mouth injury
items.desc: Wire poking your cheek, broken nightguard — we adapt the care to your situation.

firstaid.title: What to do while waiting for your appointment

items.advice: Rinse gently with warm water. Keep the fragment if possible. Avoid very hot or cold foods on the affected area.
Take an over-the-counter painkiller (ibuprofen or acetaminophen). Avoid heat on the area. Call us.
Never try to drain an abscess yourself. Rinse gently with salt water. Seek emergency care — an untreated infection can spread quickly.
Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root. Rinse it gently without scrubbing. Store it in cold milk or saline. Come within the hour — replantation success drops rapidly after 30–60 minutes.
Keep the crown safe. Do not try to reglue it with super glue. Call us for an urgent appointment.

items.q: Can I walk in without an appointment for an emergency?

items.q: How much does an emergency visit cost?
items.a: Emergency consultation fees are similar to a regular visit. We accept card, cash, and direct billing to most private insurance plans. The Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) also covers certain emergency procedures.
We are available Monday to Thursday from 9 am to 6 pm and Friday from 9 am to 2 pm. Outside these hours, leave a voicemail at 514 528-1587 — we call you back as a priority at opening.

items.q: My tooth was knocked out — what should I do immediately?
items.a: Handle the tooth by the crown, never the root. Rinse it gently without scrubbing the root. Store it in cold milk or saline. Call us immediately — the chances of successful replantation drop rapidly after 30 to 60 minutes.

items.q: Do you treat children in emergencies?

items.q: How do I know if I have a dental abscess?
items.a: Signs of an abscess include: intense throbbing pain, swelling of the gum or cheek, persistent bad taste in your mouth, fever, and sensitivity to pressure or heat. An untreated abscess can spread — seek emergency care.

items.q: Do you work with insurance for emergencies?
items.a: Yes. We offer direct billing with most private insurance providers. Bring your insurance card and we submit the claim directly. We are also a registered Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) provider.

items.q: How do I get to the clinic in an emergency?

urgence-quoi-faire.meta_title: Dental Emergency on the Plateau: What to Do? | Plateau Montreal
urgence-quoi-faire.meta_description: Broken tooth, abscess, toothache on the Plateau Mont-Royal? Learn what to do in each situation. Dr. Barchichat's guide — call 514-528-1587.
urgence-quoi-faire.hero_title: Dental emergency on the Plateau-Mont-Royal: what to do?
urgence-quoi-faire.hero_subtitle: A practical guide from Dr. Saul Barchichat on how to react quickly to a dental emergency.
urgence-quoi-faire.intro: A dental emergency rarely comes at a convenient time. Sudden pain, a tooth broken at dinner, a swollen abscess on a Monday morning — each situation calls for a rapid, appropriate response. As a dentist on the Plateau Mont-Royal for over 35 years, here are the tips I give my patients to help them get through a difficult moment and preserve their tooth.

sections.body: Rinse your mouth with warm water to remove debris. If the fracture exposes the pulp (sharp pain from air or cold), cover the tooth with dental wax or a temporary cap available at the pharmacy. Collect any fragments if possible and call your dentist immediately — ideally within 24 hours.
list: Rinse with warm water
Cover the fractured tooth with dental wax
Avoid hard or sugary foods
Call 514-528-1587 for an emergency appointment

sections.body: This is the situation that demands the fastest response. Hold the tooth by the crown (never the root), rinse gently without scrubbing, and reinsert it into the socket if possible. Otherwise, store it in milk or between your cheek and gum. Every minute counts: a tooth reimplanted within 30 minutes has an excellent chance of survival.
list: Never touch the root
Rinse gently and reinsert if possible
Store in milk otherwise
See a dentist within 30 minutes ideally

sections.body: An abscess is a bacterial infection that can spread quickly. Typical signs: intense, throbbing pain, swollen cheek, fever, bad taste in the mouth. Never lance an abscess yourself. Rinse with warm salt water for temporary relief, and seek emergency care. If you have a fever or difficulty swallowing, go to the hospital emergency room.
list: Never lance the abscess yourself
Rinse with warm salt water every 2 hours
Take a pain reliever (ibuprofen) for discomfort
See your dentist the same day

sections.body: Pulpitis is inflammation of the dental pulp often caused by advanced decay. The pain is typically sharp, persistent and worsened by heat or cold. Ibuprofen is generally more effective than acetaminophen for this type of pain. Avoid placing aspirin directly on the gum — it can burn the tissue. A root canal is often necessary.
list: Take ibuprofen (unless contraindicated)
Avoid hot and cold on the tooth
Never apply aspirin directly on the gum
Seek care promptly — a root canal can save the tooth

sections.body: If your crown falls off, keep it carefully. You can temporarily reattach it with temporary dental cement available at the pharmacy. Never use Super Glue. Avoid chewing on the affected side and call your dentist to schedule an appointment within the next couple of days.
list: Keep the dislodged crown
Temporarily reattach with pharmacy dental cement
Avoid chewing on the affected side
Call your dentist within 48 hours

faq.q: Do you see emergency patients without an appointment on the Plateau?
faq.a: Yes. At Centre Dentaire du Plateau, we reserve daily time slots for emergencies. Call us at 514-528-1587 as soon as we open and we will do everything we can to see you the same day.

faq.q: What are your emergency hours?
faq.a: We are open Monday through Thursday from 9am to 6pm and Friday from 9am to 2pm. For emergencies outside these hours, call 514-528-1587 and follow the voicemail instructions.

faq.q: Is dental emergency care covered by Quebec health insurance?
faq.a: The RAMQ generally does not cover dental care for adults. However, many group insurance plans and the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) cover a portion of emergency care. Check your policy and feel free to call us to verify your coverage.

faq.q: Can dental emergencies be prevented?
faq.a: In many cases, yes. A preventive visit every 6 months allows cavities, weaknesses and signs of infection to be detected before they become emergencies. Athletes should also wear a mouthguard during contact sports.

faq.q: My child received a blow to the face and a tooth is loose — what should I do?
faq.a: See a dentist immediately. A loose baby tooth is generally not reimplanted, but a loose permanent tooth can often be stabilized if you act quickly. Call us at 514-528-1587.

implant-guide-complet.meta_title: Dental Implant in Montreal: Complete Guide, Cost & Timeline | Plateau Montreal
implant-guide-complet.meta_description: Everything you need to know about dental implants in Montreal: cost, treatment duration, ideal candidates. Dr. Barchichat's guide, Plateau Mont-Royal.
implant-guide-complet.hero_title: Dental implant in Montreal: complete guide, cost and timeline
implant-guide-complet.hero_subtitle: Everything you need to know before getting started, by Dr. Saul Barchichat.
implant-guide-complet.intro: A dental implant is today the closest tooth replacement to a real tooth. Unlike a bridge or removable denture, it integrates directly into the jawbone and provides unmatched stability, comfort and aesthetics. Here is what I systematically explain to my patients at the Plateau Mont-Royal before starting implant treatment.

sections.body: A dental implant is a titanium screw (or zirconia for patients with metal sensitivity) surgically inserted into the alveolar bone to replace the root of a missing tooth. An abutment and a custom crown are then attached to the implant. The result is indistinguishable from a natural tooth both visually and functionally.
list: Lifespan: 15 to 25 years with proper care
Material: grade IV titanium or zirconia (metal-free option)
Success rate: 95 to 98% according to clinical studies
Preserves jawbone unlike a bridge

sections.h2: Who can receive a dental implant?
sections.body: Most healthy adults are good candidates. However, some factors may require prior preparation: smoking (slows healing), uncontrolled diabetes, bisphosphonate therapy (osteoporosis treatment) or significant bone loss. In the last case, a bone graft may be needed before implant placement.
list: Adults with good general health
Completed bone growth (generally 18 years old)
Satisfactory oral hygiene
Diabetic or smoking patients can be treated with precautions

sections.h2: Treatment steps: how long does it take?
sections.body: Implant treatment takes place in several phases. Generally count 3 to 6 months from start to placement of the final crown.
list: Consultation and assessment (panoramic, cone beam if needed): 1 visit
Extraction of remaining tooth if necessary: 1 visit
Surgical placement of the implant: 1 visit (under local anesthesia)
Bone healing (osseointegration): 2 to 4 months
Abutment placement and impression: 1 visit
Final crown placement: 1 visit

sections.h2: Cost of a dental implant in Montreal
sections.body: The total cost of a dental implant in Montreal generally ranges from $2,500 to $4,500 per tooth, including surgery, abutment and crown. This amount may be higher if a bone graft is needed. Although more expensive upfront than a bridge, an implant is often more economical over 20 years as it does not require replacing adjacent teeth.
list: Implant + crown: $2,500 to $4,500 per tooth
Bone graft if needed: $500 to $1,500 additional
Some insurance plans cover 50% of prosthetic care
CDCP may cover a portion for eligible patients

sections.h2: Implant vs bridge: which to choose?
sections.body: A bridge is faster and generally less expensive upfront, but it requires shaping healthy adjacent teeth and does not preserve bone. An implant preserves the integrity of neighboring teeth, maintains bone volume and offers a far superior lifespan. For a healthy patient, an implant is almost always the best long-term solution.

faq.q: Is the procedure painful?
faq.a: Implant placement is done under local anesthesia. During the procedure, you should feel nothing. In the 48 hours that follow, moderate pain and slight swelling are normal. Common analgesics (ibuprofen, acetaminophen) are generally sufficient to control discomfort.

faq.q: How long does an implant last?
faq.a: With good hygiene and regular check-ups, an implant can last 20 to 25 years, or even a lifetime. The porcelain crown may need to be replaced after 15 to 20 years due to normal wear.

faq.q: Does my insurance cover implants?
faq.a: Many dental insurance plans cover 50% of prosthetic care up to an annual maximum. Check your policy. The Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) also provides coverage for certain prosthetic procedures depending on your income.

faq.q: Can multiple implants be placed simultaneously?
faq.a: Yes, it is possible to place multiple implants in the same surgery, reducing the number of visits and overall recovery time. We will evaluate your situation at the initial consultation.

rcsd-eligibilite-2026.hero_title: Canadian Dental Care Plan 2026: are you eligible?
rcsd-eligibilite-2026.hero_subtitle: Everything you need to understand about the CDCP to benefit at Centre Dentaire du Plateau.
rcsd-eligibilite-2026.intro: Launched by the federal government, the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP) allows millions of low- and middle-income Canadians to access covered dental care. As a registered CDCP provider clinic, we submit claims directly on behalf of our patients. Here is everything you need to know to find out if you qualify and how to take advantage of it.

sections.h2: Who is eligible for the CDCP?
sections.body: To be eligible for the CDCP in 2026, you must meet all three of the following conditions:
list: Be a Canadian resident
Not have access to private dental insurance
Have an adjusted family net income below $90,000

sections.h2: What level of coverage based on your income?
sections.body: Coverage varies based on your adjusted family net income. The lower your income, the higher your coverage.
list: Under $70,000: 100% of covered services (no co-pay)
Between $70,000 and $79,999: 60% coverage
Between $80,000 and $89,999: 40% coverage
$90,000 and above: not eligible

sections.h2: What services are covered by the CDCP?
sections.body: The CDCP covers a wide range of preventive and basic oral health services.
list: Dental exams and X-rays
Cleanings and scaling (preventive hygiene)
Fillings for cavities
Tooth extractions
Basic root canal treatments
Dental prostheses (partial and complete dentures)
Basic periodontal care
Dental emergencies

sections.h2: How to benefit at Centre Dentaire du Plateau?
sections.body: The process is simple. At your appointment, let our team know you wish to use your CDCP coverage. We verify your eligibility directly online and submit the reimbursement claim on your behalf. Nothing more is required from you.
list: Bring your health insurance card (RAMQ)
Mention CDCP when booking your appointment
Our team verifies your coverage on-site
We submit the claim directly to Sun Life

faq.q: How do I enroll in the CDCP?
faq.a: Enrollment is done online at the Service Canada website or by phone at 1-833-537-4342. You will need your social insurance number and income information. Once enrolled, you will receive a coverage card.

faq.q: Does the CDCP cover dental implants?
faq.a: The CDCP covers certain prosthetic procedures depending on your situation. Implants are not systematically covered, but alternative prostheses (partial, complete dentures) may be. Contact us for a personalized assessment.

faq.q: I have workplace insurance — can I still benefit from the CDCP?
faq.a: No. If you have access to private dental insurance through your employer or spouse, you are not eligible for the CDCP, even if that insurance only provides partial coverage.

faq.q: Can my child be covered by the CDCP?
faq.a: Yes. Children can be covered under the family CDCP coverage if the family income qualifies. There is no minimum age.

invisalign-vs-broches.meta_title: Invisalign or Braces: Everything to Know Before Choosing | Plateau Montreal
invisalign-vs-broches.meta_description: Invisalign vs traditional braces? Full comparison: effectiveness, price, duration, maintenance. Dr. Barchichat's honest advice, Plateau Mont-Royal dentist.
invisalign-vs-broches.hero_title: Invisalign or braces: everything to know before choosing
invisalign-vs-broches.hero_subtitle: A thorough comparison by Dr. Saul Barchichat to help you make the right choice.
invisalign-vs-broches.intro: The question comes up often in consultations: should I choose Invisalign or traditional braces to straighten my teeth? Both options work well, but each has advantages and limitations depending on your clinical case, lifestyle and budget. Here is my honest answer after years of orthodontic practice on the Plateau Mont-Royal.

sections.body: Invisalign uses a series of clear plastic aligners, custom-made from a 3D digital impression of your teeth. Each aligner is worn 20 to 22 hours per day for 1 to 2 weeks, then replaced by the next one. A complete treatment includes between 12 and 40 aligners depending on case complexity.
list: Virtually invisible day-to-day
Removable for eating and brushing
Comfortable (no wires or brackets)
Digital tracking with final result visualization before start

sections.body: Braces remain the gold standard for complex cases: severe malocclusions, significant rotations, bite problems. They are permanently attached to the teeth and cannot be removed, ensuring continuous orthodontic force 24 hours a day. Ceramic braces offer a better aesthetic than traditional metal braces.
list: Ideal for complex cases
No risk of forgetting to wear
Metal or ceramic (more discreet option)
Require monthly adjustments and rigorous hygiene

sections.body: Here are the main criteria to compare based on your personal situation.
list: Aesthetics: Invisalign wins (nearly invisible) vs braces (visible, ceramic as a compromise)
Comfort: Invisalign wins (no mucosal irritation) vs braces (possible irritations)
Complex case effectiveness: braces win vs Invisalign (limits on significant rotations)
Hygiene: Invisalign wins (removable) vs braces (harder to clean around brackets)
Price: comparable — expect $4,000 to $8,000 for both options
Duration: similar — 12 to 24 months depending on complexity

sections.body: Invisalign works very well for mild to moderate misalignment in motivated patients who can commit to wearing the aligners. Braces are preferred for severe cases, younger patients, or those who may not wear aligners long enough. A consultation is essential to determine which option is best suited to your specific dentition.

faq.q: What is the cost of Invisalign on the Plateau Mont-Royal?
faq.a: An Invisalign treatment typically costs between $4,500 and $7,500 depending on complexity. This amount includes 3D planning, all aligners and retainer trays at the end of treatment. Some insurance plans cover orthodontics up to a certain maximum.

faq.q: At what age can orthodontic treatment begin?
faq.a: Orthodontic treatment can start once permanent teeth are in place, generally around age 11–13. However, adult orthodontics is equally effective — there is no upper age limit. More and more patients aged 30 to 50 are choosing Invisalign.

faq.q: Is Invisalign treatment painful?
faq.a: Slight discomfort is possible when changing aligners, usually for 1 to 2 days. This is a normal pressure indicating teeth are moving. This discomfort is generally lower than with traditional braces.

faq.q: What happens after orthodontic treatment?
faq.a: A retention phase is essential after any orthodontic treatment to maintain results. We make custom retainer trays to wear at night. Without retention, teeth naturally tend to return to their original position.

detartrage-pourquoi.meta_title: Dental Scaling: Why Twice a Year? | Dental Hygienist Plateau Montreal
detartrage-pourquoi.meta_description: Is dental scaling twice a year really necessary? Our dental hygienist from Plateau Mont-Royal explains tartar, gingivitis, and the importance of prevention.
detartrage-pourquoi.hero_title: Why dental scaling twice a year is essential
detartrage-pourquoi.hero_subtitle: The explanation from our dental hygienist at Centre Dentaire du Plateau.
detartrage-pourquoi.intro: It is one of the most common questions we hear at the clinic: "I haven't been to the dentist in a couple of years — is that a problem?" Often, the answer reveals that the patient has not been seen for 2 or 3 years. Dental prevention — particularly professional scaling — is the best way to keep your mouth healthy and avoid costly treatments.

sections.h2: What is tartar and why is it problematic?
sections.body: Dental plaque is a bacterial film that forms naturally on your teeth after every meal. If not removed through regular brushing and flossing, it mineralizes within 24 to 72 hours to form tartar (dental calculus). Once calcified, tartar can no longer be removed by brushing — it requires professional scaling.
list: Tartar irritates the gums and causes gingivitis
Left untreated, it progresses to periodontitis (severe gum disease)
Periodontitis is the leading cause of tooth loss in adults
Links have been established between periodontal disease and heart disease

sections.h2: What is a professional dental cleaning?
sections.body: During a scaling (or dental prophylaxis), our hygienist uses ultrasonic and manual instruments to remove supragingival (above the gum) and subgingival (below the gum) tartar. The treatment also includes polishing tooth surfaces and personalized hygiene advice. The appointment lasts approximately 45 to 60 minutes.
list: Ultrasonic scaling (comfortable and effective)
Subgingival scaling for deep areas
Polishing to remove surface stains
Personalized brushing and flossing advice

sections.h2: Why twice a year and not once?
sections.body: The recommendation for two visits per year is based on the time it takes tartar to accumulate to a clinically significant level — generally 6 months. Some patients (smokers, diabetics, people with a history of periodontitis) may need up to 4 cleanings per year. Conversely, patients with perfect hygiene and little tartar may only need to visit once a year. Your hygienist will adjust the frequency to your situation.

A professional cleaning twice a year typically costs $100 to $200 per visit. By comparison, treating advanced periodontitis (root planing) can cost $800 to $2,000, not counting the extractions or implants that may follow. Prevention is clearly the most cost-effective investment for your dental health.
list: Prevents gingivitis and periodontitis
Detects cavities at an early stage (less treatment needed)
Reduces the risk of long-term tooth loss
Far less expensive than curative care

faq.q: Does scaling hurt?
faq.a: For the majority of patients, scaling is not painful. Some sensitivity is possible if the gums are inflamed or if there is heavy tartar buildup. We use ultrasonic instruments that minimize discomfort, and we can apply a numbing gel if needed.

faq.q: Is my cleaning covered by insurance?
faq.a: The vast majority of dental insurance plans cover 2 professional cleanings per year at 80-100%. The CDCP also covers preventive hygiene care for eligible patients.

faq.q: Do I need a cleaning even if my teeth don't hurt?
faq.a: Absolutely. Most serious dental problems (deep cavities, periodontitis) are asymptomatic in their early stages. Waiting until something hurts usually means waiting until the problem is much more severe — and much more expensive to treat.

faq.q: Does an electric toothbrush replace professional scaling?
faq.a: No. An electric toothbrush is excellent for removing plaque daily, but it cannot remove calcified tartar. Only a professional with appropriate instruments can do that.

blanchiment-pro-vs-maison.meta_title: Professional vs At-Home Teeth Whitening: The Truth | Plateau Montreal
blanchiment-pro-vs-maison.meta_description: Professional teeth whitening or at-home kit? Effectiveness, safety, lasting results. Dr. Barchichat's honest take, dentist on Plateau Mont-Royal.
blanchiment-pro-vs-maison.hero_title: Professional vs at-home teeth whitening: the truth
blanchiment-pro-vs-maison.hero_subtitle: Which option is truly effective, safe and long-lasting? Dr. Barchichat's take.
blanchiment-pro-vs-maison.intro: Teeth whitening is the most requested cosmetic treatment in the office. With the proliferation of kits sold at pharmacies, grocery stores and even on Instagram, confusion is widespread. Here is what I tell patients who ask me: "Doctor, is it worth paying more for professional whitening?"

sections.body: The active ingredient in all whitening products is peroxide — either hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide which breaks down into hydrogen peroxide. This molecule penetrates tooth enamel and breaks down colored pigments embedded in the dentinal tubules. The concentration of peroxide and the application time determine effectiveness.
list: Professional products: 25 to 40% hydrogen peroxide
Pharmacy kits: 6 to 10% peroxide (EU/Canada regulatory limit)
Over-the-counter products (strips, pens): 1 to 3% — very limited effectiveness
Activated charcoal, baking soda: abrasive, do not chemically whiten

sections.body: At the office, we offer two complementary approaches. In-chair whitening (Zoom or Beyond type) uses a high concentration of gel activated by LED light for 60 to 90 minutes. Take-home whitening uses custom trays with a lower concentration gel worn 2 to 4 hours per day for 2 to 3 weeks. Both methods can be combined for maximum results.
list: In-chair whitening: visible results from the first session (3 to 8 shades)
Custom trays: gradual and lasting results
Protective gel on gums to prevent irritation
Included follow-up: before and after assessment with Vita shade comparison

sections.body: Pharmacy kits (Crest, Colgate Optic White, etc.) are safe and can produce mild results on surface stains. But their concentration is limited by Canadian regulation, and universal trays don't fit your dentition perfectly — which reduces gel contact with teeth and increases the risk of gum irritation. Expect a maximum of 1 to 2 shade changes.
list: Limited effectiveness (1 to 2 shades vs 3 to 8 in office)
Non-custom trays (less effective)
Risk of gingival irritation if poorly fitting
Less lasting results (6 to 12 months vs 18 to 36 months in office)

sections.h2: Who can have their teeth whitened?
sections.body: Whitening is safe for healthy tooth enamel. It is contraindicated during pregnancy and breastfeeding, on teeth with untreated active cavities, and on restorations (crowns, veneers, fillings) which do not whiten. A prior assessment is essential to ensure your teeth and gums are in good health before starting.

faq.q: Does teeth whitening damage enamel?
faq.a: No, when done correctly with appropriate concentrations. Twenty years of clinical studies show that peroxide whitening, used as directed, causes no lasting damage to enamel. Temporary post-treatment sensitivity (24 to 48 hours) is normal and reversible.

faq.q: How long do the results last?
faq.a: Professional whitening typically lasts 1 to 3 years depending on your consumption of coffee, tea, red wine and tobacco. Annual touch-ups with custom trays make it very easy to maintain results.

faq.q: Does whitening work on crowns or veneers?
faq.a: No. Porcelain, composite or zirconia restorations do not respond to whitening agents. If you want to harmonize the color of your natural teeth with your restorations, this should be discussed with your dentist before treatment.

faq.q: What does professional whitening cost on the Plateau Mont-Royal?
faq.a: In-office whitening typically costs between $400 and $700 depending on the type of treatment (single session or custom trays). This price includes the pre-treatment assessment, follow-up and maintenance trays. Most insurance plans do not cover cosmetic treatments.
